clue.text: Struggle in street, teeming

blocks.note: ST is the standard abbreviation for street
rife means abundant, swarming

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out on a crowded street.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is conflict or bitter disagreement, a synonym for a struggle between parties.

clue.text: Put up with bad rugby player

blocks.note: to stand something is to tolerate it
food that is off has gone bad

explanation.surface: Tolerate a poor rugby player.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the stand-off, or fly-half, plays between the scrum-half and the centres.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-off is a position in rugby, so the word names one of the team's players.

clue.text: Polish girl's contagious disease

blocks.note: to polish is to rub
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman from Poland has an infectious illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Polish with its capital P pretends to be the nationality; it is the verb meaning shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubella, or German measles, is an infectious viral illness.

clue.text: Bush's note about changing history

indicators.note: changing signals that the word after it alters its letter order
about means around, so the note wraps the rearranged letters

blocks.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A US president's memo on rewriting the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Bush's capital B suggests the American president; it is a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsythia is a shrub that bears bright yellow flowers in early spring.

clue.text: US port bombed in blackout

indicators.note: something bombed is blown apart, so the letters before it are scattered and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American harbour city is bombed during a wartime blackout.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a wartime blackout of lights; the definition means a loss of consciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed, near-unconscious state, close in meaning to a blackout of the senses.

clue.text: Quartermaster-sergeant, somewhat brusque

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of something, so the letters are a portion of the longer word

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two halves

explanation.surface: An army quartermaster-sergeant is rather curt.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse means abrupt and short in speech, a synonym for brusque.

clue.text: Clown making mistake almost breaks mine

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off
to break into something is to enter it, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: an error is a mistake
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A clown slips up and nearly causes a collapse in a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the stock sad clown of French pantomime, in white face and loose costume.

clue.text: Live in one end of Poplar, East End?

indicators.note: one end of a word is its first or last letter; here it is the last

blocks.note: last letter of Poplar
E is the abbreviation for East
an end of something is one of its sides

explanation.surface: Living in Poplar, a district of London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Poplar is an area of East London; East End reads as the district but splits into a compass point and a word for a side.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to live or dwell somewhere permanently.

clue.text: Argue violently about extremely bizarre tavern

indicators.note: doing something violently throws it into disorder, so the word it follows is rearranged
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outermost letters are kept
about means surrounding, so one set of letters wraps around the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then shuffled
the first and last letters of bizarre

explanation.surface: Two people quarrel fiercely about some very strange pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters split after the second letter to take in the two ends of bizarre.
explanation.definitionFit: An auberge is a French inn, a roadside place offering drink, food and lodging, like a tavern.

clue.text: Enthusiastic worker brewed average beer

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so the following letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A keen employee made some ordinary ale.
explanation.definitionFit: An eager beaver is an idiom for a very keen, hardworking person.

clue.text: Surgical instrument causing panic, initially, in the services

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word it follows
one element is placed inside the other, as the word in says

blocks.note: the armed services are the forces
first letter of panic

explanation.surface: A surgeon's tool sets off alarm among military personnel.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letter of panic sits inside the armed forces, just before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceps are pincer-like tongs used by surgeons for gripping tissue, so they are a surgical tool.

clue.text: Cries of "wolf" as a ram fell awkwardly on top of Sinai

indicators.note: falling awkwardly leaves things jumbled, so the preceding letters are rearranged
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of Sinai

explanation.surface: A ram tumbles on Mount Sinai, prompting shouts of wolf.
explanation.walkthrough: The added S joins the anagram fodder before everything is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying wolf, from Aesop's fable, means raising warnings that turn out to be baseless, which are false alarms.

clue.text: Daughter and partner dawdle

blocks.note: D is the usual abbreviation for daughter
an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.surface: A girl and her companion take their time.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally is to waste time or linger, a synonym for dawdling.

clue.text: Info given by staff about mature garden plant

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word wraps around the one that follows

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
mature in the sense of aged
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Employees pass on information about a fully grown flower in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is informal British for the facts or the low-down; it surrounds the word for aged, then the stick follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldenrod is a tall perennial with plumes of yellow flowers, often grown in borders.

clue.text: Nobody showing anxiety about the Welsh crew

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for anxiety goes around the next word

blocks.note: fear is dread or anxiety
taken as written
W is the abbreviation for Welsh
a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: An unimportant person worries about the Welsh team.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing crew, a common crossword equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: A featherweight figuratively is someone of little importance or influence, which is what a nobody is.

clue.text: Troop member showing guile with grid construction?

indicators.note: a construction is something built from parts, so the letters are assembled anew

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier shows cunning in building a grid, perhaps for a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: Troop suggests soldiers, but Guides are also organised in troops or companies.
explanation.definitionFit: A Girl Guide belongs to the youth movement for girls, organised in units once called troops.

clue.text: Exclamation made by pop star dropping round

indicators.note: dropping means letting something fall away, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: Boy George is the singer of Culture Club
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A singer shouts something as he drops a round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: By George is a mild, old-fashioned oath expressing surprise.

clue.text: Climbing plant may give gypsies pleasure

blocks.note: travellers is a term for itinerant people, including gypsies
joy is delight or pleasure

explanation.surface: A climbing plant might delight wandering people.
explanation.definitionFit: Traveller's joy is the common wild clematis, a scrambling vine of hedgerows.

clue.text: Sleeveless garment in basin by cap

blocks.note: a tank is a container, like a basin
a cap is a top or lid

explanation.surface: A sleeveless top left in a washbasin beside a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank top is a sleeveless knitted pullover worn over a shirt.

clue.text: It's featured in fetish for unarmed combat

indicators.note: featured in means appearing inside, so the first part sits within the second

blocks.note: taken as written
juju is a fetish or charm in West African belief

explanation.surface: Someone has an obsession with fighting without weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: Fetish means an object worshipped for magic power, not an obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: Ju-jitsu is a Japanese martial art of fighting without weapons, using holds and throws.

clue.text: Select church on river, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the river name is taken by its sound

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: Pick a church beside a river, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, including one through York.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose is to pick out or select from alternatives.

clue.text: Transfers DS inside royal house

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the two letters go into the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
the House of Hanover was a British royal dynasty

explanation.surface: A detective sergeant is moved into a royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: DS looks like Detective Sergeant but is just two letters; Hanover is the dynasty of the four Georges and Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands over means passes or gives to someone else, the same as transfers.

clue.text: Flowing robes, muted in colour

indicators.note: flowing implies movement and change of shape, so the letters rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Loose, flowing gowns in subdued colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Sober applied to colours means plain and subdued rather than bright.

clue.text: Enlisted US soldier, good one - ordinary bloke

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
I is the Roman numeral for one
an ordinary Joe is an average man

explanation.surface: A private in the American army is a decent, ordinary guy.
explanation.definitionFit: GI Joe is the nickname for a typical enlisted soldier in the US army.

clue.text: A month round Connecticut - temperate, no sun

indicators.note: no sun means the letter standing for sun is dropped from the word before it

blocks.note: O is round in shape
CT is the postal abbreviation for Connecticut
temperate means abstemious, sober
S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: A month's mild, sunless weather in Connecticut.
explanation.walkthrough: Temperate looks like a weather word but means abstinent from drink here.
explanation.definitionFit: October is the tenth month of the calendar year.

clue.text: Dram in brandy glass

blocks.note: first meaning: a small alcoholic drink
second meaning: a balloon glass with a narrow top

explanation.surface: A measure of spirit poured into a balloon glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a small tot of liquor and the bulbous glass that brandy is served in.

clue.text: Judge newly headed this large organisation

indicators.note: newly headed says the word gets a different first letter in place of its old one

blocks.note: an umpire judges a game

explanation.surface: A judge has just taken charge of this big organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of the word for judge is swapped for a new one; the clue does not say which letter, so the definition settles it.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is an extensive enterprise or group of businesses under one control, a large organisation.

clue.text: Pass up rubbish

blocks.note: first meaning: decline, turn down
second meaning: waste, garbage

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: re-FUSE the verb and REF-use the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to decline an offer; as a noun it means waste material.
